items.title: If in doubt, delete the uv.lock file
items.summary: I've been getting the occasional confusing Python dependency error since switching over to Python 3.15 and the rule I'm having to remember is: If in doubt, delete the uv.lock file Most of my projects are libraries which don't include a uv.lock file, since it's rude for a library dependency to lock versions for anything else that uses it. Running uv run pytest etc tends to leave uv.lock files lying around, which are listed in .gitignore and so do not get committed to my repositories. items.title: Why a 660-ton ball makes Taipei 101 safer
items.summary: Why does Taipei 101 hang a 660-ton ball near the top? The ball is 5.5 meters across, built from 41 layers of steel plate, each 12.5 centimeters thick, and the official site puts it at 660 metric tons. It hangs on cables, and when wind pushes the tower one way, the ball swings against it. That's called a tuned mass damper. The official site says its main purpose is to reduce the swaying of the tower during strong winds. Same weight, but free to swing, it protects the building. Idea and structure: Mark Rober's Short "How To Keep a Skyscraper From Falling Over". Sources are in the pinned comment....

items.title: datasette-llm 0.1a9
items.summary: Release: datasette-llm 0.1a9 I have some big upgrades to Datasette Agent in the pipeline, but in the meantime here's a tiny user experience improvement to the underlying datasette-llm plugin. It now picks up the default model used by LLM , which means you can start using Datasette Agent without needing to explicitly configure a default model: uvx --with datasette-agent datasette content.db --internal internal.db Previously you would also need to specify a model with -s plugins.datasette-agent.default_model gpt-6-astra . Tags: datasette , llm , datasette-agent
